The Army continues to march forward with industry to meet its Unified Network effort goals, aligning the enterprise and tactical network programs to reduce network complexity and provide greater tactical mobility to support the Army’s division-centric warfighting at echelon. TEM 13 panelists discussed the efforts’ progress and pending milestones with industry attendees, providing updates on how the UN will underpin all modern network capabilities, including critical cyber security efforts such as Zero Trust. (U.S. Army Reserve photo by Spc. William Kuang)
WASHINGTON — The Army is poised to take its next step toward potentially unleashing defensive AI agents on its networks, as plans to award contracts to two companies by the end of the week, a key official said.
“The one that we plan to award on Friday is our take action element. So essentially, how are we not only autonomously detecting a potential adversary? How are we now doing something — having an autonomous response within prescribed parameters of a human operator, or even in conjunction with that?” Brandon Pugh, the service’s principal cyber advisor, said at the annual AUSA conference on Monday. “That is extraordinary. Something we haven’t done and we’re very excited about.”
Pugh declined to provide the names of the awardees ahead of the Friday announcement.
The network AI effort, dubbed Project Griffin , stemmed from a tabletop exercise with top industry executives and service leaders. The Army published a commercial solutions opening in August, spurring 108 submissions that were narrowed to 10 finalists.
Pugh explained that the Army has tools, such as its Panoptic Junction capability, that he said have a nearly 90 percent success rate at identifying malicious activity on the network. But they don’t currently have a way at remediating or remedying those threats, especially with limited humans.
Despite the award on Friday, officials said agents won’t begin work on government networks immediately.
“For us, it’s going to be: Are we as humans ready to let the agent actually take action? You think about that for how many years a human has been the person making the patch, remediating something, so we’re walking ourselves through what does it mean to have an agent to do that work and then how do you check that agent’s work. So a lot still to do in this space,” Lt. Gen. Christopher Eubank, commander of Army Cyber Command, told reporters at the conference.
He added that the service is working with companies to understand where what they can do in this space and determine what does it actually mean to take action, noting they’re working “hand in hand with the companies to build out what it looks like” and then put it through a deliberate process on the Army’s portion of the network. The two companies awarded could work in tandem on the effort or do their own thing.
Pugh said that using a commercial solutions opening to gather ideas was actually suggested by members of industry, as a way to keep responses broad as opposed to prescribing what companies should provide to the Army. Industry oftentimes has capabilities or ideas that aren’t even on the government’s radar, he said.
Given the big aperture, the Army wants to figure out what the companies are capable of providing as they put it through its paces.

1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R Is Now an 833-Piece Mattel Brick Shop Set That Can Be Customized
14 photos
Photo: Mattel
Slowly but surely, Mattel’s newest side business, the so-called Brick Shop, continues to grow with the addition of new cars that can be built at scale, in as-accurate-as-possible form. After the two Hondas announced at the beginning of the year, the Civic EF and S2000, it’s now time for another major Japanese nameplate to do the same.
Taking advantage of the 2026 Paris Motor Show that opened its doors this week, the toy maker announced the launch of a replica of the 1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R, or, as it’s known in some circles, the Hakosuka.
Trying to stay as close as possible to the vehicle that’s considered by many the reason why the GT-R grew to become the icon that it is today, Mattel worked on the project with its Hot Wheels brand to create a 1:16 scale replica.
The miniature Nissan comes together after no less than 833 pieces of interlocking plastic bricks are properly put together and, when complete, appears decorated with the classic white racing livery with printed red stripes.
There are some functional elements included in the design, including a functional steering wheel and an opening hood that lifts out of the way to reveal a replica of the Nissan’s engine, a piece of hardware that comes with detailing, but no working parts.
The very interesting thing about this design, the result of the first-ever collaboration between Mattel and Nissan, is that it has been created with customization in mind. More specifically, fans can choose to install a custom decal sheet, one of two wheel cover sets (one of them made in metal), and a bunch of extra parts, including a front splitter, headlight covers, and an intercooler.
Officially titled the Mattel Brick Shop x Hot Wheels 1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R , the set will become available in stores in January 2027, and it will sell for $59.99 to anyone over the age of ten. For that, the toy maker also throws in a metal signature plate and an exclusive, matching, 1:64 scale Hot Wheels die-cast toy.
Aside from the Nissan performance car announced today, Mattel already offers through the Brick Shop models from a large number of carmakers, including, in no particular order, Audi, Lamborghini, Maserati, Mercedes-Benz, Acura, Chevrolet, Honda, Cadillac, Aston Martin, and Toyota.
As for what models can be had in this form, you can think about the likes of the Cadillac Project GTP Hypercar, Maserati MC20, 1968 Chevrolet Camaro, Mercedes-Benz 300 SL, Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport, and 1990 Acura NSX.
All of these vehicles, no matter the series they’re part of, come as exact scale replicas of the real-world cars and trucks. Unlike competitor LEGO, which generally steers clear of using metal parts, Mattel’s sets do include them wherever and whenever possible.

Chittagong port © Asmtamanna |
By Bangladesh correspondent
13 October 2026
Bangladesh has signed a $336m loan agreement with China to expand and modernise Mongla port, as workers at the country’s main container gateway of Chittagong threaten an indefinite hunger strike over a deal handing a major terminal to DP World.
Signed in Dhaka on Sunday, the loan will fund the construction of two container jetties, as well as a cargo and delivery yard, at Mongla, alongside the purchase of modern port equipment, with expectations of an increase in annual capacity of 394,000 teu.
Dhaka-based garment exporter Rafayet Ullah said construction of the Padma Bridge would make Mongla a genuine alternative to Chittagong, telling The Loadstar: “The increased number of jetties and modern equipment means the port will be able to facilitate significant volumes.”
The China-backed expansion comes as authorities in Bangladesh face opposition from port workers over a decision to award DP World a 15-year concession to operate Chittagong’s largest container terminal, the New-mooring Container Terminal (NCT).
Signed on 8 October, extending the concession, the agreement has seen workers and members of left-wing political parties stage mass “symbolic” hunger strikes outside the port as they demanded the deal’s cancellation. And now they plan more drastic action.
Humayun Kabir, coordinator of the Port Protection Sangram Parishad, said that, with government authorities refusing to discuss the deal, workers were “giving the government another bout of time. If the deal is not cancelled, we will go on a ‘fast unto death’ on 19 October”.
Mr Kabir cited other countries, including Djibouti, where port agreements involving DP World had been cancelled, calling for the same outcome in Bangladesh, while colleague Ibrahim Khokon said they had not been adequately informed about the deal before it was signed.

Leaked Documents Point to HEMI-Powered Dodge Charger Comeback
17 photos
Photo: Dodge
Gearheads have been dreaming of this moment since Dodge pulled the plug on the HEMI and the models that came with it back in 2023. Stellantis is reportedly planning the comeback of the HEMI V8 under the hood of the Dodge Charger. The new-gen Charger is currently sold only as an EV and as an ICE powered by the Hurricane inline-six.
Stellantis is desperately trying to win back muscle car purists. It hasn’t had a proper muscle car since it killed the previous-generation Charger and Challenger, for which former CEO Carlos Tavares is supposedly responsible.
But Tavares abruptly resigned in December 2024, making room for car guys to become executives back again. The new Stellantis CEO, Antonio Filosa, has repositioned internal combustion engines at the core of the company’s turnaround strategy.
Furthermore, soon after Carlos Tavares's departure, Tim Kuniskis was back in the game, following a short-lived retirement, as the head of Dodge. Later on, he was appointed the head of Stellantis's American Brands.
Photo: Dodge Kuniskis is the man who orchestrated the revival of the SRT division and the return of the HEMI back into the Ram trucks, after Stellantis had pulled the plug on the TRX and its V8-powered siblings in 2023. Following this move, Ram went from rags to riches within a year.
Gearheads expect him to do the same with the Dodge brand. Ram truck sales in the United States are up 20% year-to-date through September 2026, with 369,379 units sold compared to 307,701 during the same period in 2025.
The demand for the 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee has been exceptionally high. The initial allocation was sold out almost instantly. When order banks opened, the entire 2026 calendar-year production allocation sold out in just 90 minutes .
The return of the HEMI in the Dodge lineup would most likely have a similar effect on sales figures. In the meantime, the automaker is struggling, with just 8,796 total units sold in the United States through the first nine months of 2026.
Photo: Dodge Fueled by the inline-six twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter Hurricane engine, the gas-powered Charger SIXPACK moved 3,446 units in Q3 2026. Only 233 customers went home with a Charger Daytona . That is a devastating drop of 92% from the 2,776 units sold during the same period in 2025.
Dodge advertises the range-topping Charger Daytona as the most powerful muscle car in the world, which it is not. Not even by a long shot. At 670 horsepower (679 metric horsepower), the Charger Daytona Scat Pack is short on power compared to the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC with its 795 horsepower (806 metric horsepower) and the Mustang GTD with 815 horsepower (826 metric horsepower).
Besides, the Ford Mustang remained the only V8-powered purebred muscle car on the market, making the rules in a league of its own, after Dodge discontinued the Charger and Challenger and Chevrolet retired the Camaro back in 2023.
The EV is no consolation for the HEMI diehards, even though it comes with the Fratzonic Chambered Exhaust, engineered to mimic the growl of the HEMI. " It sounds like an angry mosquito ," purists protested on social media the first time they heard it in a video teaser. Can't blame them…
Photo: Dodge But now, Stellantis is getting ready to give them the real deal. Automotive News reports that Stellantis is planning a supercharged V8 engine variant of the Dodge Charger to boost struggling sales. According to internal planning documents, the automaker intends to resurrect the iconic 6.2-liter HEMI for the eighth-generation Charger.
The company has already informed suppliers that it intends to build around 12,000 HEMI-powered Chargers per year. Production is scheduled to begin at the end of 2027, with the almighty Charger hitting the market as a 2028 model year. Internal documents indicate that the V8 will be offered with both body configurations, the two-door coupe and the four-door sedan.
Unlike the current Charger powered by the Hurricane inline-six, operating in an all-wheel-drive setup, the upcoming V8 Charger is being developed as a traditional rear-wheel-drive vehicle, which means that the ZF eight-speed automatic transmission will put the power down through the rear wheels in pure muscle car fashion.
The move represents a major course correction for the brand. Dodge has tried to silence consumer interest, but it can no longer ignore it and now has to completely rethink its powertrain strategy. Engineers are currently working to adapt the STLA Large architecture, designed from the beginning to handle multiple powertrains, to fit the large HEMI V8.
Photo: Dodge In the meantime, Stellantis is officially treating the project as " purely speculation ," according to a spokesperson from the brand, who refused to comment " on future product strategy, " as revealed by Automotive News.
Despite the official silence, Dodge CEO Matt McAlear previously hinted at the possibility : " Don't be surprised if it would fit, " he said. Nobody would be surprised. Just glad that it is finally happening.

Lectric eBikes has spent the last several years steadily expanding from its original folding fat-tire e-bikes into just about every corner of the affordable electric bicycle market. Now the company is returning its attention to the commuter category with the new Lectric XPress Lite, a lighter and more affordable version of its popular XPress2 urban e-bike.
Priced at $1,099 , the XPress Lite takes the general formula of the more powerful XPress2 and pares it down into a lighter, more nimble package aimed squarely at everyday city riders. Lectric describes the new model as prioritizing portability and agility rather than the heavier-duty performance of the XPress2.
For those who prioritize a solid ride over raw power, the intuitive and smooth torque sensor matched with modest but not over-the-top power will feel right at home.
And at 45.6 lb (20.7 kg) with the battery removed, it certainly lands on the lighter end of Lectric’s lineup – a key feature for those needing to lift the bike into a car or carry it up stairs. It’s not an ultralight e-bike by conventional bicycle standards, but for an affordable, full-size commuter e-bike with this level of equipment, that’s a fairly manageable figure.

Power comes from a 500W nominal rear hub motor that peaks at 864W and produces just over 61 Nm of torque. That motor gets paired with an eight-speed Shimano Altus drivetrain and, importantly, an in-house-designed torque sensor. Lectric also includes its XPerience Switch system, allowing riders to switch between torque-sensor and cadence-sensor operation.
That last feature is particularly interesting at this price. Torque sensors have become increasingly common on affordable e-bikes, but giving riders the ability to choose between the more natural bicycle-like response of a torque sensor and the easier, more relaxed operation of a cadence sensor offers the best of both worlds.
While I personally prefer the natural pedal feel of a good torque sensor, those who want to get more oomph out of their motor without having to lean too hard into the pedaling will appreciate the cadence sensor. That’s perfect for anyone with mobility issues who wants to remain active but might not have the same pedaling strength as higher-performance riders.
The bike can be configured for Class 1, 2, or 3 operation where local laws permit, and includes five pedal-assist levels plus an under-the-bar, paddle-style thumb throttle.
Hydraulic disc brakes handle stopping duties, while the 27.5 x 1.95-inch puncture-resistant street-oriented tires come pre-Slimed from the factory. That factory-installed tire Slime means that riders likely won’t even realize how many fat tires they didn’t get, since the Slime takes care of sealing tire punctures before they can become a problem.
There’s also a 3.5-inch color TFT display and an integrated rear light with brake-light and turn-signal functionality.
The biggest compromise appears to be battery capacity. The 7.8 Ah battery packs in 375 Wh of capacity and is rated for up to 45 miles (72 km) of range on pedal assist, though as usual, expect real-world range to depend heavily on assist level, terrain, rider weight, speed, and other conditions. Both the complete e-bike and its battery carry UL certifications, keeping up with ever-evolving requirements and adding more peace of mind for riders.
And while it might be a smaller battery than many premium e-bikes these days, the budget-focused $1,099 price means riders are making up for it with extra value. Lectric has plenty of models with twice as much battery capacity as this one, and thus the Lectric XPress Lite is likely positioned more for riders who favor the low-cost, low-weight, high-efficiency approach of smaller battery commuter e-bikes. And considering my daily driver e-bike has the same sized battery and still nets me around 43 miles (70 km) of range on pedal assist, the Xpress Lite’s 375 Wh battery will still likely be plenty for many riders.
The XPress Lite is now available in four colors – Toasted Marshmallow, Pine Green, Glacier White, and Stratus White – and Lectric offers the usual laundry list of accessories, including racks, fenders, panniers, a suspension seatpost, comfort saddle, mirrors, phone mount, and more. All color options use the same mid-step frame, striking a balance between rigidity and accessibility with a frame that is easier to mount by swinging a leg through the center.
The new model also helps fill another niche in what has become an impressively broad Lectric lineup . The Phoenix-based company first made its name with the wildly popular XP folding e-bike series, but has since expanded into cargo bikes, trikes, full-size commuters, lightweight folders, and other models designed around different types of riders. In fact, just about the only type of bike they don’t make is a unicycle, and at this point, I wouldn’t be too surprised to see one land in my inbox.
A diversity of offerings has been one of Lectric’s strengths: instead of simply making its original bike more expensive and more sophisticated every year, the company has continued branching outward at relatively approachable price points.
At the same time, Lectric has leveraged its industry connections and buying power as the largest e-bike maker in North America to help launch the new premium e-bike brand, Monarc, offering higher performance and higher-shelf components that stick to Lectric’s signature affordable pricing ethos.
The XPress Lite feels like another example of that diversification-for-value strategy. Not everyone needs a monster motor, huge battery, fat tires, or a 70-pound e-bike. For riders who primarily want an affordable commuter that’s easier to carry up a few stairs, maneuver through an apartment building, or simply pedal around town, shaving weight and price can be every bit as useful as adding more power.
At $1,099 , the XPress Lite looks like Lectric’s attempt to prove that sometimes less e-bike is actually more.

The Ever Lotus. Photo: Buggi Porschien
By Alison Koo
13 October 2026
Transpacific container freight rates are likely to remain higher than on Asia-Europe for some time, as stronger economic conditions in the US support import demand and weaker European growth weighs on cargo volumes and freight rates.
Evergreen general manager Wu Kuang Hui said the rate divergence had become increasingly pronounced: “strong on US routes, weak on Europe routes”.
And he said on Friday he expected the stronger US market to continue supporting transpacific rates at a premium to Asia-Europe rates, and there was “no reason to be pessimistic” about the US routes before the lunar new year 2027 as “there are record-high import volumes at several major US ports, low inventory levels, and optimistic consumer demand”.
US imports from the Far East have grown about 5.1%, but volumes to Europe have increased more rapidly, by 12.2%. However, the weaker European economic backdrop has translated into reduced pricing power on Asia-Europe trades.
European spot volumes have increased significantly, but freight rates that surged in April, following the US-Iran conflict, have declined steadily since July.
On Friday, the Shanghai Containerised Freight Index showed Shanghai-US east and west coast rates relatively stable, at $10,524 and $7,584 per 40ft, respectively. Shanghai-Europe rates continued to decline, losing 3%, to $2,274 per teu.
The gradual return of container vessels to the Red Sea and Suez Canal is adding further downward pressure on Asia-Europe rates by restoring effective capacity. Although geopolitical risks in the Red Sea have not been fundamentally resolved, carriers are increasingly resuming the routings.
By contrast, transpacific capacity remains supported by robust US import demand. Mr Wu noted that US spot rates were significantly higher than negotiated rates in Q4 last year, and expects long-term contract prices next year to exceed this year’s.
Potential US tariff adjustments could provide additional support.
Mr Wu said: “Importers could receive about $160bn in tax rebates, potentially allowing lower end-product prices and higher inventory levels, which could stimulate further imports.
“The US outlook is not without risks. A potential inflation-driven interest-rate hiking cycle could eventually weaken terminal demand, making the second quarter of next year less certain. Nevertheless, we expect the near-term outlook to remain favourable.”
Meanwhile, congestion is helping absorb capacity across both trades. Singapore’s port utilisation has exceeded 90%, while severe congestion at Shanghai and Ningbo has contributed to vessel bunching and schedule delays.
Evergreen’s strong market outlook comes amid a sharp increase in the carrier’s revenue. In September, consolidated revenue reached TWD49.7bn ($1.56bn) up 64% year on year, while cumulative revenue for the first nine months of 2026 rose 15%, to TWD338.4bn ($10.61bn).
Mr Wu said booking conditions through November were expected to remain favourable, followed by another seasonal increase in December, ahead of Chinese New Year.
Evergreen operates 242 vessels with capacity of 2.04m teu, giving the seventh-largest shipping line a 5.9% market share. The Taiwanese operator plans to expand the fleet to around 290 vessels, 2.74m teu, by 2030.

Perseverance Rover Breaks the Record for Total Distance Driven on Another Planet
24 photos
Photo: NASA
28.10 miles, or 45.22 kilometers. That’s what the odometer of NASA’s most recent rover to travel to Mars, Perseverance, showed on October 11. That’s a tiny distance, if you consider that it took the two-wheeler five and a half years to get there, but still the new record for total distance ever driven by any machine on any alien world.
The Perseverance landed on the Red Planet in early 2021, tasked with several missions, including the search for signs of past life. To accomplish them, the rover had to constantly move from place to place and, in doing so, became the new record holder.
The distance Perseverance covered by October 11 was enough to place it in front of the Opportunity, which, from 2004 to 2018, moved 28.06 miles (45.16 km). Even more interesting, though, is the fact that the new vehicle keeps on moving, and, at the end of its life (nobody knows when that will be), it would probably have set a pretty difficult record to beat.
The achievement announced by the American space agency this week can only be fully appreciated if one looks back at what all the previous Mars rovers achieved. Only this way can one fully appreciate what a long way Martian rovers have come since the first one touched down almost three decades ago.
Photo: NASA/JPL Back in 1997, NASA’s first Mars rover, the microwave-oven-sized Sojourner, spent 83 Martian days on the job, during which time it covered just 330 feet (100 meters). Then, the Spirit and Opportunity twins, having landed on the Red Planet in 2004, spent six and 15 years on the job, and covered 4.8 miles (7.7 km) and 28.06 miles, respectively.
The fourth NASA Mars rover, Curiosity , has clocked 23.65 miles (38.07 km) since landing in 2012, but, seeing how this machine is still operational, that will probably not be the end of its journey and its story.
If you change perspective, the numbers above paint the picture of Perseverance needing five and a half years to cover the same distance achieved by Opportunity in almost 15 years. And, strangely enough, that’s not owed to an increase in speed (the Perseverance can cover 1,351 feet or 412 meters each Martian day), but to the new rover’s self-driving capabilities, bundled together in something called the AutoNav.
The operation of the Perseverance goes a bit like this: controllers here on Earth set destinations and select waypoints the rover must pass through, but leave it up to the AutoNav to plot the best and safest course to each of them.
Photo: NASA The autonomous navigation system does this by imaging the terrain as the rover moves and creating a 3D map of potential hazards that must be avoided, using no less than 600,000 measurement points. Mind you, this real-time navigation and decision-making process takes place even when the rover travels at or near its top speed. The rover is thus capable of steering less and rolling more, while also checking its position against orbital maps.
NASA revealed that about 90 percent of the total distance covered so far was driven with the help of AutoNav . An earlier version of the solution, installed on the Opportunity and Spirit rovers, was responsible for only about five percent of the distance traveled by the two.
The record-holding rover is presently moving toward an area of the Red Planet called Idubi, moving through Lac de Charmes on the western rim of Jezero Crater, which is its landing spot. According to the people running it, all systems are still fully operational.
Knowing this, NASA recently extended, for the first time, the rover’s mission life duration and cleared it to keep going at least until 2028. On a hardware level, NASA said at the end of last year, it could live until at least 2031.
Photo: NASA Although the record-breaking distance the machine reached, and the prospect of going much, much further, are reasons enough to celebrate, there is something even more exciting in traveling far on another world: it gives the rover and its handlers the opportunity to explore areas of the planet that we’re not necessarily included in the science plan at first.
For a life-hunting tool, that’s probably more precious than anything, and it has already proved its merits. In its travels, the rover moved from an ancient lakebed into a fossilized river system, then onto the crater rim. In doing so, it uncovered a potential biosignature in a place called Cheyava Falls.
The discovery is so important that NASA says this is the closest we have ever come to finding life on Mars. Work on getting a better understanding of the finding is still ongoing, after NASA made the details public as it seeks help to either confirm or refute the finding.
Meanwhile, the Perseverance is heading to Idubi in a bid to prove or disprove the existence in the planet’s past of hydrothermal systems. After that, it targets the Rainbow Falls, a 328 feet (100 meters) block of crust uplifted by the impact that created Jezero four billion years ago.

An open fundraising window, retreating policy pressure and a soaring biotech stock index are bringing a fresh breath of air across the biopharma world as the sector heads into the third quarter earnings reporting period.
Potential deals and launch execution will be the tale of the quarter, analysts have declared. In terms of M&A, the industry has already exceeded 2025’s tally of $136 billion across 57 deals, Truist Securities wrote at the end of September. Many potential takeout targets have undergone a re-rating, which means rising valuations could stir up dealmaking behind the scenes.
“We note the sector’s cheap optionality—the names trading below cash, and the outsized takeout premiums that defined 2025—has largely been priced out, which to us reflects re-rated targets and not cheaper assets,” Truist Securities wrote last week.

Buyers will increasingly be looking to validated biotech targets with near-term data readouts plus differentiated profiles, Truist said.
As always, Johnson & Johnson will kick off the earnings period, with a conference call scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 13 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Here, we look ahead to a handful of company announcements that analysts will be watching carefully.
How is RevMed’s Rasonque launch going?
Truist is watching a few names closely heading into the fourth quarter. Top of the list is Revolution Medicines, which will likely be able to claim the biggest success story of 2026. The company’s pancreatic cancer medicine finally broke through the intractable disease, swiftly earning an FDA greenlight after doubling survival in a Phase 3 trial.
Now, RevMed will be reporting initial launch numbers for the therapy. Truist expects the Q3 report to include about $14 million in initial sales for the drug, now known as Rasonque. This falls just short of the consensus estimate of $20 million. Nevertheless, the launch has so far been heralded a success by analysts, including Truist.
If the trajectory continues, RevMed, with its first approved medicine, could be on the way to $100 million or more in sales for this year, according to Truist.
Key opinion leaders have been bullish on the therapy, informing Truist that all available patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma are getting access to treatment with no payer pushback. The firm therefore boosted expectations for 2026 from $102 million to $113 million. Back in September, Truist projected $13.8 billion in peak revenue for Rasonque.

Credit: Saudia Cargo
By Alex Lennane
13 October 2026
Saudi Arabia has lost almost a third of its international air cargo capacity over the past three days, as Riyadh’s airport shutdown disrupts shipments and heightened airspace risks complicate routing options.
Rotate data captured today shows combined inbound and outbound capacity on freighters and widebody passenger aircraft across Saudi Arabia down 33% against the equivalent 72-hour period a week earlier, a decline of 3,537 tonnes, to 7,292 tonnes.
At Riyadh, capacity across all airlines, excluding narrowbody passenger aircraft, fell 99%, from 3,925 tonnes to just 26 tonnes.
The latest notice to airmen for King Khalid International Airport states that the aerodrome is unavailable, due to precautionary measures until 9pm UTC on 17 October.
Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said yesterday it had extended the suspension while authorities completed checks on the safety and operational readiness of airport facilities. It did not specify a reopening date.
Airline suspensions could prolong the capacity squeeze even after the airport reopens: Air France-KLM has suspended Riyadh services to the end of October; Etihad’s Abu Dhabi–Riyadh flights are cancelled until 19 October, according to Reuters ; and Delta has postponed the launch of its Atlanta–Riyadh service from 23 October to March 2027, delaying an additional source of belly capacity.
Oman Air has confirmed that some Saudi-bound shipments are waiting in Muscat following cancellations.
“The KSA situation has so far mainly impacted some planned passenger flights into RUH where we have cancelled services in line with airport closure,” Mike Duggan, head of Oman Air Cargo, told The Loadstar . “We have a small amount of cargo waiting in MCT as a result.”
Mr Duggan said the airline’s planned Saudi road feeder service was still being developed, although continued disruption could accelerate its introduction.
“It has not impacted our RFS services so far, as the KSA element for our RFS is still in planning stage – perhaps it may give us some impetus to start sooner if the situation remains.”
He added that Oman Air Cargo had otherwise experienced limited impact to date and continued to monitor developments.
Forwarder Expeditors has identified road transport among alternative routing options for affected shipments. Its 9 October advisory noted suspended Riyadh services by Saudia Cargo and restrictions affecting several other cargo carriers, but did not quantify diverted freight or identify replacement gateways.
The disruption also raises questions for flights passing through Saudi airspace without landing.
EASA’s conflict-zone bulletin, revised on 9 October, recommended avoiding two defined areas of Saudi airspace at all altitudes, and exercising caution throughout the remainder of the Jeddah flight information region. It highlighted risks from missiles and drones, interception activity, falling debris, and the potential misidentification of civil aircraft during air defence operations.
Saudi airspace forms part of a southern Europe-Asia corridor through Egypt and onwards to Oman or the UAE, identified in OPSGROUP’s 6 October operational assessment.
Further avoidance could increase flight distances and fuel requirements, potentially reducing cargo payload on weight-constrained services.
For Saudia Cargo, the shutdown comes during a fleet expansion. Saudia’s international freighter and widebody belly capacity fell 19% over the past three days, to 7,410 tonnes.
Saudia Cargo carried 573,000 tonnes in 2025, approximately 0.8% below its 2024 total. Its partnerships to develop Asia–Europe connectivity through Zhengzhou and Riyadh could disrupt connecting shipments, alongside Saudi imports and exports.
Four new 777 freighters are scheduled for delivery between this month and May 2027, under a purchase-and-leaseback agreement with DAE, adding capacity just as the carrier faces uncertainty over operations at its key gateway.

50,000 Showed Interest in Jaguar's Most Polarizing Car Yet, the Type 01, Many Have Never Owned a Jag
10 photos
Photo: Jaguar
Jaguar has recently unveiled the production version of its most polarizing car that has ever borne the brand’s logo, and it has had to deal with backlash and praise both. The endurance is paying off. Jaguar executives have revealed that they have received 50,000 expressions of interest for the electric grand tourer, and most of them come from people who have never owned a Jaguar before.
Two years ago, Jaguar announced plans of rebranding and unveiled the Type 00 concept car, which was unlike anything built by the automaker before. The model attracted tons of backlash as well as sudden departures from the company of people who were supposed to orchestrate the revival.
Former chief designer Gerry McGovern was escorted out of his office earlier this year, after rumors about his departure had been circulated for months, but Jaguar dismissed them, saying he wasn’t going anywhere. It turns out that he was.
Furthermore, Jaguar's CEO Adrian Mardell stepped down after having spent 35 years with the company and three years in the position. In his place came P.B. Balaji , the former Chief Financial Officer of Jaguar's parent company, Tata Motors.
Photo: Jaguar Nearly a year later, Jaguar is counting its blessings with a wave of new buyers and alienating its oldest loyalists, because four in five prospective customers interested in the new Type 01 have never owned a model of the brand before. The British house labels this as proof that its new strategy is a success.
" We've never had over 50,000 people say to us 'I'm really interested in what you’re doing. We call this KMIs (Keep me informed), so we talk to them on a regular basis ," Jaguar managing director Rawdon Glover revealed in a conversation with Australian publication Drive. Glover says the response has validated the automaker’s decision to move into a higher price bracket.

2026 Cisco AI Infrastructure OCP Pre-Briefing Final Slide 10: Cisco and NVIDIA USFP 400G optics
Ahead of the OCP Global Summit, Cisco briefed analysts on AI-infrastructure announcements spanning optics, silicon, systems, and software. For us, the headline is clearly the ultra-dense small form factor, or USFP, a pluggable module Cisco developed with NVIDIA for 400G SerDes lanes, which it says enabling higher-density 1.6Tbps fabrics. Cisco also detailed the Silicon One G300 in first systems, a G302 front-end top-of-rack switch coming in Q4 2026, and the Silicon One A100L aimed at lower-cost 10G/1G out-of-band management switches. USFP will be a big one with both Cisco and NVIDIA behind it and because next-generation pluggable optics are a key part of the 1.6Tbps Ethernet generation. To me, the A100L stood out on the briefing call since Cisco’s custom silicon applied to cost-sensitive switching rather than only the high-performance fabric.
Cisco OCP AI Networking Announcements
Cisco and NVIDIA are designing a new pluggable form factor for 400G SerDes lanes rather than today’s common 200G lanes. We will say “common” because there is still a lot of 56G PAM4 SerDes and 112G gear being sold today. Moving to 400G means 1.6Tbps networking can happen on four lanes, scaling to 6.4T aggregate across 16 lanes and 12.8T across 32. Cisco and NVIDIA are jointly drafting the multi-source specification so other vendors can build to it.
2026 Cisco AI Infrastructure OCP Pre-Briefing Final Slide 10: Cisco and NVIDIA USFP 400G optics
It is interesting that QSFP/ OSFP were not sufficient for the next-gen speeds. Pairing that optics work with switch silicon produces the ethernet-to-optical architecture on the next figure, which places the Silicon One G300 in first-shipped Cisco 8000 and N9000 systems at 102.4T of capacity across 1.6T ports. Now, the new G302 drives a 51.2T front-end top-of-rack switch using 200G SerDes.
2026 Cisco AI Infrastructure OCP Pre-Briefing Final Slide 11: Cisco AI Ethernet and optical architecture
The Silcon One A100L made me ask a question at the analyst pre-brief. Custom AI silicon usually appears in high-performance fabric switches since that is where the value from doing something custom often can be captured. Lower-end silicon found in management boxes running the 1G/10G networks in racks tends to be mostly just a volume play. Cisco said it was proof the architecture scales and hyperscale clients wanted to run SONiC on everything. I asked what the licensing model would be, more perpetual like a C1300 or more like the Nexus 9K series but did not get a clear answer on that one so I am going to call it a TBD. The reason I asked is that if you are doing custom silicon versus like a Marvell Prestera and not capturing software revenue, that feels like a tough road to take.
Live Protect for Cisco SONiC on Nexus One adds runtime vulnerability shielding to N9000 switches, applying policy to a running system so operators can protect it before scheduling a conventional patch and reboot. Cisco SONiC is set to be available in 2027, but that feels like a big move for Cisco as well.
2026 Cisco AI Infrastructure OCP Pre-Briefing Final Slide 23: Cisco Live Protect for SONiC
Cisco positions Live Protect to shrink the exploit window, with availability slated for Q2 2027 in Cisco-validated SONiC environments. Customers will also be able to choose between community or custom SONiC and a Cisco-validated distribution, as the final operating-model figure shows.
2026 Cisco AI Infrastructure OCP Pre-Briefing Final Slide 24: Cisco SONiC operating model options
Rounding out the software story is how Cisco intends customers to run SONiC. An operating-model figure lays out two tracks. A community or custom path offers full customization and source access for maximum control, while a turnkey Cisco-validated path provides a defined upgrade path and professional services. Notably, Cisco’s use of NVIDIA Spectrum-X is an option we have covered before, but aside from supporting the open-source SONiC, Cisco is also supporting switching platforms from NVIDIA.
Final Words
With Cisco and NVIDIA behind USFP, it will become an industry standard. Hopefully we will get to see some module shells on the OCP show floor this week. Silicon One G302 is a meaningful milestone on its own, but A100L sliding into out-of-band management feels almost crazy to me, since the sub-1Tbps switch space was widely assumed to be largely commoditized.

Kia's New EV2 Crossover Just Took Five Euro NCAP Stars
8 photos
Photo: Euro NCAP
Presently the most affordable Kia BEV available in Europe, the EV2 is one of the safest small crossovers out there. The newcomer left Euro NCAP's testing facilities with five stars, and it did so as the least expensive vehicle tested by the safety boffins on this occasion.
Euro NCAP splits automotive safety into four categories: Safe Driving, Crash Avoidance, Crash Protection, and Post Crash Safety. The B-segment crossover, which is listed with a kerb weight of 2,565 kilos (5,655 pounds) by the not-for-profit organization from Belgium, earned 74, 66, 86, and 89 percent across them.
The organization credits the coveted overall result to the strong results in Safe Driving and Crash Protection, which is another way of saying that Kia could have done better in other areas. But first, let's talk crash test performance. In the offset test, where the driver's side takes the impact against the barrier, the front passenger's chest came back marginal. Everything else was rated either adequate or good.
The rear-impact sled found a different weak spot, that being whiplash protection for the driver and rear passengers, confirming that a softly sprung commuter box pays for its posture when rear-ended. Also labeled as an aggressive impact partner in a frontal collision, the EV2 was deemed solid in terms of highway behavior due to nicely calibrated lane keeping and collision detection.
In junction-crossing scenarios, however, it scored 14 percent. Euro NCAP found it worse still in junction-turning cases, where the EV2 scored a big fat zero. As far as dooring is concerned, which credits a warning before the rear passenger flings the door open, the little Kia managed a pitiful 25 percent.
Photo: Euro NCAP For a small crossover that will spend plenty of time on tight, narrow streets, that result is certainly disappointing. Inside, the EV2 ran the table on ergonomics, receiving full marks for driving controls, comfort, and infotainment. Under the 2026 rule that wants indicators, wipers, hazards, the horn, and the eCall button as direct physical inputs, the EV2 secured the only clean sweep of the latest Euro NCAP batch of vehicles.
Driver monitoring also received praise, and Euro NCAP was also impressed with the speed assistant's capability to identify the correct limit most of the time over nearly 2,000 kilometers (1,243 miles) of real-world driving through Italy, Germany, and Austria. When it comes to pedestrian protection, head protection scored 67 percent for a struck cyclist and 55 for an adult pedestrian.
The high and flat fascia is understandably kinder to a rider than a walker, and Euro NCAP further noted mixed results for pelvis protection. In a vehicle that also targets young families, Child Presence Protection is marked by the organization as not being available at all.
Everything that occurs after the crash otherwise scored well, including the provisions for cutting occupants out quickly and the automatic high-voltage electrical system shutdown. The Euro NCAP's five-star overall rating applies to both the 42.2-kWh battery and the 61-kWh pack in both left- and right-hand drive.
Over in Germany, which is the largest market for new vehicles in Europe, the South Korean automaker wants 26,600 euros at the very least for the EV2. The United Kingdom has it a little worse with its base EV2 specification, which is 27,995 quid before options.

Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) is investing more than $500 million to expand U.S. manufacturing , with projects in Idaho, Washington, Indiana, and North Carolina scheduled between 2026 and 2028.
What’s Related
The company makes electronic devices that protect, monitor, and control electric power systems. In its Oct. 8 announcement , SEL said demand is growing as customers invest in electric utilities, grid upgrades, data centers, and industrial infrastructure . The plan includes new factories, conversions of existing buildings, and expanded assembly operations.
Several projects were announced earlier, including facilities in Nampa and Post Falls, Idaho, and the purchase of a former building supply property in Pullman, Washington.
Where SEL is expanding
SEL outlined six facility projects, with operations or completion expected in 2027:
Moscow, Idaho : More than $70 million for a new, 305,000-square-foot electronic device factory, expected to be operational by the end of 2027.
Nampa, Idaho : A $150 million investment in property, equipment, and people to convert a 103,000-square-foot building into an electronic device factory. Operations are expected to begin in early 2027, with 250 employees initially.
Post Falls, Idaho: A $150 million investment in property, equipment and people to convert a commercial building into an electronics factory. Operations are expected to begin in late 2027, with 250 employees initially.
Pullman, Washington : Conversion of a 135,810-square-foot building on an 11.5-acre property into a manufacturing operation. The facility is expected to open in early 2027 and employ about 300 people.
West Lafayette, Indiana: A $25 million expansion of board assembly operations, expected to increase production by more than 35%.
Charlotte, North Carolina: A $15 million expansion adding more than 50,000 square feet of custom panel assembly space.
The earlier Nampa announcement said the factory will make electronic devices similar to those produced at SEL’s existing factories in Pullman and Lewiston, Idaho. SEL President Dave Whitehead said the expansion would help reduce lead times and increase production.
According to the company, the approximately 300 employees will include existing SEL employees and new hires. The building previously housed a hardware store, warehouse , and lumberyard.
More equipment, shifts, and manufacturing workers
SEL is also investing more than $100 million in manufacturing equipment. Along with more than 600 additional assemblers and new shifts in Pullman and Lewiston, the company expects electronic device output to rise by an estimated 40% to 60%.
The employee-owned company has also raised manufacturing starting wages to attract and retain workers. In its August wage announcement , SEL set starting pay at $26 an hour for day shifts, $31 for swing shifts, and $36 for night and weekend shifts, effective Aug. 16.
Those increases followed an April adjustment that raised the manufacturing starting wage to $21.50 an hour. SEL said the additional pay is intended to help it hire and retain the workers needed to meet customer demand.

V6-Only 2027 Nissan Patrol Starts Production in RHD for the Australian Market
10 photos
Photo: Nissan
As with the Armada and the Infiniti-branded twin for the United States of America, the Patrol for Australia loses V8 oomph in favor of a more sophisticated V6. Gifted with twin snails, the sixer in question is the only engine confirmed for the right-hand-drive 2027 Nissan Armada due in Aussie showrooms next year.
Coming to dealers in the first quarter of 2027, the Y63 in right-hand drive rolls off the Nissan Shatai Kyushu plant's assembly line. Although the Japanese automaker controls nearly half of it, said facility operates as a contract manufacturing base for the Yokohama-based automaker.
Nissan Shatai is used as a contract manufacturer due to legacy, asset efficiency, and manufacturing specialization. For starters, it predates Nissan as an independent car body and train manufacturer before formally joining the Nissan bandwagon in the early 1950s. Nissan does not carry 100 percent of Nissan Shatai's operational costs, and the negotiated master production service agreement allows Nissan to dial back orders without absorbing the full overhead blow.
And finally, Nissan Shantai holds the assembly expertise for body-on-frame models. By keeping body-on-frame designs separate from unibodies from the standpoint of manufacturing, the automaker is further optimizing its global operations. Having cleared all that up, right-hand-drive production was a long time in the making when you remember that the Y63 went official two years ago.
It all started with the Abu Dhabi reveal from September 2024. Two months later, the full-size model was already on sale in Middle Eastern markets. Just like in the US-market Armada, the Patrol uses the Japanese manufacturer's VR35DDTT engine. In Australian specification, it produces a hugely respectable 317 kilowatts and 700 Newton-meters in optimal conditions, namely 425 horsepower and 516 pound-feet when converting from the metric system to American English.
Photo: Nissan The Armada NISMO, which is not part of the Y63 range for the Land Down Under, belts out 460 horsepower. Even in base flavor, the sixer of the right-hand-drive Armada is 19 kilowatts and 140 Newton-meters up on the eight-cylinder lump from before. Speaking of the ol' days, the seven-speed automatic is gone as well. A nine-speed unit now comes by default, with its design based on the 9G-TRONIC from Mercedes-Benz.
Peak torque is delivered earlier in the rev range, helping the Y63 while towing or crawling over broken ground. Its ladder frame is a highlight as well, incorporating larger side members that deliver 40 percent more torsional rigidity when compared to the Y62 generation. Stiffer means the frame resists twisting better when one wheel drops into a rut while the other remains loaded, making the suspension work more predictably off the beaten path.
The stiffer route also means less chassis flex, therefore resulting in NVH improvements over the outgoing Y62. With this new chassis, the Patrol supports up to 3,700 kilograms (8,157 pounds) of maximum braked towing capacity. That puts the Patrol ahead of the Land Cruiser 300's rating, which is 3,500 kilograms (7,716 pounds) in the Australian market.
To qualify for the advertised maximum towing capacity, the Y63 requires the Nissan genuine towbar. Also gifted with more high-strength steel in its body panels, the 2027 model is AUD 2,450 pricier than its forerunner. That is AUD 98,990 sans off-road costs, a starting price that converts to USD 69,035 today.
Six grades join the entry-level Ti, those being the Ti+, Ti-L and Ti-L+, PRO-4X, and Ti-L Reserve. As its name implies, the PRO-4X is the one to have for more serious all-terrain shenanigans. All trims get a two-speed transfer case, an electronic locking rear diff, and electric power steering instead of a hydraulic design. From the Ti-L, the standard suspension is swapped in favor of Intelligent Dynamic Damping.
The system that adjusts damping continuously, regardless of terrain, is only half the story. Both the PRO-4X and the Ti-L Reserve, which are the priciest members of the Aussie range, level up to adaptive air suspension. This suspension design enables the driver to raise the body in off-road mode, while selecting park lowers it for easier loading and entry/exit.

Harley-Davidson TRP-Onyx Is How You Give a Milwaukee-Eight Softail the Clubstyle Touch
53 photos
Photo: Thunderbike
Certain kinds of custom modifications are best suited for certain kinds of base motorcycles, as each of the two-wheelers allows for specific upgrades to be made so that the ride is not ruined, mechanically or otherwise. Yet, with enough tender love and care, and a touch of imagination, there’s almost nothing some garages in this world can’t do.
Take the clubstyle design. There is this general consensus that the best Harley-Davidson platform to use this style on is the Dyna - and that’s true, as we’ve seen countless mind-blowing projects based on that come to light over the years.
And we’ll probably continue to see some more, as even if the frame is no longer in production, there are plenty of bikes using it still around. But that doesn’t mean that change is not on its way.
For a while now, custom garages have started reimagining the Harley Softail bikes in all sorts of ways, including clubstyle. And here’s the perfect example that a Harley-Davidson Low Rider S can just as easily adopt that look.
The motorcycle you’re looking at now, born in Harley’s factories back in 2023, was modified by German custom shop Thunderbike into a clubstyle machine that’s now called TRP-Onyx. That’s short for Thunderbike Racing Performance and a reference to the black color scheme that was wrapped over it.
As usual, the crew did not tamper with the bike’s frame or engine, so we’re still dealing with the Softail frame that holds a Milwaukee-Eight 117 engine good for 106 hp and 169 Nm of torque. But most of everything else was thrown out and replaced.
The list of performance parts used on the build is impressive, to say the least, and it includes the bike’s wheels (now sized 21 inches at the front and 18 inches at the rear), the swingarm, and the triple clamps.
These elements are blended with specific clubstyle components, including the handlebars, risers, and mirrors. A number of Thunderbike covers have been pulled over all the components that need shielding, while Brembo braking hardware is on deck to handle stopping needs.
Surprisingly enough, the Harley-Davidson TRP-Onyx did not look the way it does now when it was first introduced three years ago. Back then, it featured a lot of parts in gold, and that helped it win that year’s Professional class in the Clubstyle Europe Contest.
As usual, Thunderbike does not say how much money went into the entire project , but the parts that have been fitted onto the two-wheeler are worth an estimated $13,000. That’s not including the man-hours spent on putting it together, the paint job, and, of course, the base Low Rider S. And that could easily put the total cost of the build at around $50,000.

Not every business needs a conventional van to carry whatever they need transporting from point A to B. Some businesses also need a vehicle that is comfortable enough for long driving hours on a daily basis, as well as a vehicle whose footprint is small enough for the most urban of jungles.
Volvo has an answer to said requirements in the form of the EX30 Cargo, which is best described as a small crossover whose rear seats have been removed for additional cargo room. Converted for small commercial vehicle duties, the full-electric model now qualifies for the Zero Emission Van Grant in the United Kingdom.
Applying the £2,500 discount, you get a starting price of £33,529 on the road. Introduced in March 2026, the UK-market EX30 Cargo targets people who need a bit of usable load space without giving up the comfort of a passenger vehicle.
Beyond the rear bench's removal, the EX30 further boasts a black-painted bulkhead that separates the cabin from the cargo area. Modified rear side panels also need mentioning, and the doors have been modified to allow extended access to the cargo area. Of course, mounting points and cargo area illumination are standard as well.
The underfloor subframe customers don't see is key to said mounting points and the 390-kilogram payload, which can be alternatively read as 860 pounds. Volvo 's UK subsidiary further lists up to 1,000 liters (or 35.3 cubic feet). Based on these figures, you will realize that EX30 Cargo is not a replacement for compact vans.
This vehicle, instead, makes a lot of sense for small deliveries, service visits, and mobile workers whose daily kit fits in a smaller cargo area than you get from the likes of the Ford e-Transit Courier and Citroen e-Berlingo. Simply put, call it a niche commercial vehicle.
Photo: Volvo Over in the United Kingdom, the government recognizes the EX30 Cargo as a van despite not being one. The official list of eligible small electric vans also includes the Dacia Spring Cargo, which is derived from a passenger car as well. The small van grant provides up to 2,500 pounds sterling, and to qualify, a vehicle must meet three main requirements.
First and foremost, zero tailpipe CO2 emissions. The electric-only mandate continues with at least 60 miles (96 kilometers) of range without any emissions, and the final requirement is no more than 2,500 kilograms (5,512 pounds) in terms of gross vehicle weight.
A separate thing from the Electric Car Grant for passenger vehicles, the Zero Emission Van Grant is not unlimited. Per the government's web portal, only those who apply now can find out how many grants are currently available to distribute to eligible customers.
Prospective buyers are presented with two power levels, namely 150 hp for the P3 setup or 272 hp for those who upgrade to the P5. Advertised with best-in-class payload, the EX30 Cargo is good for 295 miles (475 kilometers) of range at most on a full charge in the WLTP.
Including variables like weather conditions, driving style, and payload, it goes without saying that its real-world range may be very different from what the Swedish automaker promises online.

Netradyne on Tuesday expanded the lineup of AI agents running on its Netradyne Intelligence platform. The update adds a Campaign Agent for driver coaching, a builder that lets fleet managers create their own agents, and conversational answers drawn from live fleet data. The capabilities are available to direct Netradyne customers in the U.S. and Canada.
“Fleet teams are pressed for time to configure reports and piece together answers,” said Avneesh Agrawal, CEO of Netradyne, in the announcement. “Agents give managers an easy and scalable way to draw on Netradyne Intelligence. They describe what matters and agents bring it to them, with people staying in control. The impact is already clear: customers created more than 250 agents within a month of release.”
The San Diego-based driver safety and fleet management company unveiled Netradyne Intelligence in June , built on more than 30 billion miles and 150 billion minutes of real-world driving data. Agrawal said then that fleets had invested in visibility into their operations, but “the real challenge now is execution.” Coaching and incident response agents were available at launch. Netradyne added a Collision Management Agent and an MCP connector in August .
At the June launch, Chief Product Officer Pramod Akkarachittor said the agents “reason about context, execute multi-step workflows, and follow through on behalf of managers.” Tuesday’s update lets managers decide what that work is.
Campaign Agent scores driver competitions
The new Campaign Agent turns coaching into a competition. Managers choose the safety priorities and the driver groups. The agent runs the scoring, daily standings and driver updates. Comparisons from before, during and after a campaign show where drivers improved and where they still need support.
The new agent joins two ready-made agents that Netradyne says take on fleets’ most time-consuming safety work. The Collision Management Agent handles incidents from first report to resolution. The Coaching Agent, according to the June release, identifies which drivers need attention based on goals managers set. It prepares each session with driver history, top alerts and a recommended improvement plan.
Managers build their own agents
To build a custom agent, a manager describes in plain language what it should do, such as compiling a shortlist of drivers for recognition or preparing fuel-efficiency coaching packs. The manager then picks the driver groups, conditions and schedule.
The agent delivers updated findings and recommendations in the Netradyne portal or by email. That gives each customer analysis shaped to its own priorities without rebuilding reports, the company said.
Answers from live fleet data
Managers can also ask questions about their fleet and get answers from live data. Follow-up questions dig into what changed and why, broken out by driver, group, behavior or time period. When an answer proves useful, the manager can turn it into an agent that runs on a schedule.
Those questions also work outside Netradyne’s portal. The MCP connector, which Netradyne describes as a secure bridge to fleet-specific insights, extends fleet context into AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude. Teams can ask questions and build agents inside those tools.
Netradyne will show the capabilities at the American Trucking Associations ’ Management Conference & Exhibition , which runs Oct. 17-20 at the Charlotte Convention Center in Charlotte, N.C.

The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube usually dwells around The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway or MRP (Mission Raceway Park, aka Thunder by the River, in British Columbia, Canada), but on this particular occasion they want to show us something from BMP – aka Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida, all over again.
First, let’s meet the contestants: in the left lane sits a dark gray C8 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 with a full aerodynamic package and what look like aftermarket tires and wheels. The other driver has an ‘import’ versus the domestic representative from GM, a thoroughly modified R35 Nissan GT-R sports car. It’s a classic case of mid-engine versus the front-engine RWD recipe, so let’s find out who prevails.
These two feisty rivals were present at BMP, most likely for the FL2K event, and they were surrounded by teammates and fans; that’s for sure. They took their time setting up the perfect start position, but when the green light was on, it was pretty clear that only one of them was actually paying attention. As such, one of the contestants took a decisive advantage over their rival and went home victorious with a spectacular 7.96s pass at more than 173 mph.
The other one was far behind, on the other hand, with a result of 10.58s at just 104 mph. Actually, for the latter, the scoreboard was of no consequence because more important things happened during the run : the runner-up tried to start catching up to its rival, or something bad happened mechanically, because the car started skidding away from the ideal trajectory and impacted the concrete barrier without much input from the driver, who only hit the brakes right before the impact.
Nobody knows exactly what happened there; maybe there was an oil slip or something like that, or a mechanical issue, but one thing is for sure – that car needs extensive repairs now, as it even lost a rear wheel in the aftermath of the impact. Hopefully, nobody was hurt, and only the driver’s ego got bruised. Anyway, we didn’t want to spoil the fun of watching who’s who, so let’s check out the video embedded below; it’s only two minutes long.
Also, you might want to check out the comments section, too; there’s even more drama over there than across the tarmac of the quarter-mile dragstrip! Anyway, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette, unlike the R35 Nissan GT-R, is the only one alive and well in terms of production, as the Japanese sports car went on hiatus while Nissan decides what to do next with it.

By Gavin van Marle
13 October 2026
Gemini Cooperation partners Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd are to relaunch their Far East-Middle East Loop at the weekend.
Marketed as AGX by Hapag-Lloyd and FM1 by Maersk, the service represents a fresh capacity injection for importers in the Gulf beleaguered after nearly eight months of conflict.
There is one key change, however – the Middle East call at Jebel Ali has been replaced by a call at Khor Fakkan, which, being outside the Hormuz Straits, has emerged as a key Gulf bypass port since the conflict began.
The revised port rotation will be: Qingdao-Ningbo-Tanjung Pelepas-Khor Fakkan-Singapore-Qingdao.
The service was ended on 27 March after it became clear the US-Iran conflict would last longer than initially hoped for.
“The FM1 re-launch provides customers with additional direct ocean connectivity to Khor Fakkan, while we continue to operate with the necessary precautions across the Middle East,” Maersk told customers. “Existing booking restrictions and cargo acceptance guidelines remain applicable.
“Maersk’s existing landside solutions will complement the re-launched service and ensure we are able to serve the Upper Gulf,” it added.
The switch from Jebel Ali to Khor Fakkan is part of wider trend that has, understandably, seen volumes being shipped directly to Dubai and Abu Dhabi plummet, and according to a recent Drewry analysis, is expected to herald the end of their respective transhipment volumes.
The AGX will formally relaunch with the departure of the 8,400 teu Maersk Athabasca from Qingdao on 17 October, which is now due to arrive at Khor Fakkan on 16 November, according to the new proforma schedule.
The vessel is currently deployed on Gemini’s US3 transpacific service and, according to AIS, arrived at that service’s base port, Shanghai, on Saturday.
In its previous iteration, according to Xeneta’s eeSea liner database, the service deployed eight vessels with an average capacity of 10,900 teu.
Meanwhile, freight rates on the Asia-Middle East trade have soared since the conflict began, with the latest price index – which records aggregate all-in contract and spot rates – from Container Trades Statistics (CTS) for August showing year-on-year growth of 130% on August 2025 to hit its highest ever level, CTS confirmed to The Loadstar today.
Source: Container Trades Statistics
And, according to Xeneta’s spot rate data from early September, rates to Khor Fakkan have increased an eye-watering 479% since 28 February, beating Covid-era highs, to hit $10,626 per 40ft.
“These extraordinary increases have seen spot rates on these trades surpass previous record highs set during the Covid disruption,” said Xeneta chief analyst Peter Sand. “The increased cost is in addition to longer transit times and worse reliability, but while the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to container vessels, shippers have little other option to get their goods into the Gulf region.”
Trucking landbridges to Gulf destinations have supported this transition, and volumes at Khor Fakkan have jumped as result.
“Gulftainer has taken weekly throughput from around 8,000 teu to 65,000 teu, a 700% increase, with a weekly target of 100,000 teu expected within the next month or two,” Drewry’s associate director of ports and terminals, Eirik Hooper, recently noted .
“This is a facility that was built as a transhipment terminal, so it didn’t really even have a truck gate. Every box left by sea – they’ve had to build the gate complex from nothing, and have gone from about 100 truck movements a day to 8,500.
“It’s remarkable operational achievement,” he added.
In late August, DP World revealed it had moved 500,000 teu through Gulf overland corridors since the beginning of March, and recently acquired a further 700 trucks for deployment on landbridges.

After Pfizer’s venture arm co-led Enodia Therapeutics’ $25 million seed round in January, the pharma has signed up to collaborate with the biotech on small-molecule drugs to eliminate pathogenic proteins where they’re being made.
Pfizer is putting more than half a billion dollars on the line to partner with Paris-based Enodia Therapeutics on small-molecule drugs that can destroy pathologic proteins before they manifest as diseases.
The companies did not disclose specific financial details of the agreement in their Tuesday morning release. But all told, the deal could top $500 million in value, a sum that covers an upfront commitment from Pfizer plus research, development and sales milestones. Enodia will also be entitled to certain tiered royalties on net sales.
For its investment, Pfizer will get access to Enodia’s proprietary technology to develop small-molecule drugs that target Sec61 , a membrane protein complex involved in the processing of newly made proteins and linked to a wide range of conditions, from kidney and liver diseases to cancer and even diabetes. The partners haven’t specified what specific conditions they plan to address. BioSpace has reached out to the companies for more details.
Enodia will be responsible for screening, optimizing and developing Sec61 inhibitor candidates, while Pfizer will take charge of clinical studies, as well as manufacturing, regulatory and commercial activities.
Launched in February 2025 by Argobio and The Institut Pasteur, Enodia’s work focuses on targeting Sec61 through a machine learning–driven design engine that draws from comprehensive biological libraries, according to the biotech’s website . This approach yields small-molecule drug candidates that can trigger the destruction of pathologic proteins at the point of synthesis—before they can exert their disease-causing effects.
Enodia’s approach enables the drugmaker “to inhibit disease-driving proteins while preserving essential physiological functions,” CEO Yves Ribeill said in a prepared statement on Tuesday.
Enodia is not the only biotech targeting the Sec61 secretory channel. Gate Bioscience, which last week drew another big investment in the form of a deal expansion with Eli Lilly, is also in the business of developing small-molecule drugs that eliminate target proteins by blocking their progress through Sec61.

A few weeks after the funding push, Enodia paid $1 million upfront to acquire a clutch of Sec61-targeting preclinical assets from Kezar Life Sciences—a deal designed to improve Enodia’s “understanding of Sec61 selectivity mechanisms.” Under the terms of this agreement, Enodia is on the hook for up to $127 million in development, regulatory and commercialization milestones.
For Pfizer, the Enodia deal comes amid a sweeping restructuring effort. The pharma launched its cost-cutting program in October 2023 and has since continued to raise its savings target . GM Defense Presents Rugged Chevrolet Silverado 3500 HD With No Driver Looking Like a 'Skateboard'
10 photos
Photo: GM Defense
General Motors , the largest US automaker based in Detroit, likes to dip its toes into just about everything, including military stuff, and just recently its GM Defense subsidiary came to the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) Annual Meeting and Exposition to showcase something new and intriguing.
General Motors may not be a part of the roster for the 2026 Paris Motor Show going on these days (October 12-18, 2026) at the Paris Expo Porte de Versailles in France, but it’s no stranger to big events. At least its GM Defense subsidiary, which went to the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) Annual Meeting and Exposition to present the “rapid acceleration of its global business model.”
The company says it’s guided (like a homing missile) by a “customer-first, technology-transferred” approach, as it aims to bridge the gap “between commercial innovation and tactical military deployment at unprecedented speeds.” The U.S. Army’s planned requirements have ballooned GM Defense’s Infantry Squad Vehicle order from the initial batch of 649 vehicles to no less than 12k units, mostly because of the success of their Infantry Squad Vehicle Utility (ISV-U) prototype.
The latter will be turned into a highly versatile five-soldier variant that will be fielded across 39 active-duty and National Guard mobile brigades, while its contract with Lockheed Martin for the mission-critical PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) housing components was honored just 22 days after the signing of the contract in August.
More importantly, at the event, GM Defense revealed its brand-new Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) concept, created on the basis of a rugged Chevrolet Silverado 3500 HD dual-rear-wheel model now fitted with a skateboard architecture to support silent logistics and casualty evacuation. First functional trials are coming in 2027, and GM also showcased the EPIQ Hybrid prototype, a customer-inspired 60-kilowatt/100-kilowatt-hour expeditionary energy storage system paired with an onboard generator.
It was created to “lower thermal and noise signatures in austere environments,” while subsidiaries like GM Defence UK will advance their own programs – the latter company has the Light Mobility Vehicle program proposal made together with Team LionStrike with NP Aerospace and BAE Systems, focusing on a low-risk, high-quality, commercially based solution operating at the speed and scale required by the allied forces.
“The modern defense landscape demands advanced capability, rapid fielding and sustainable scale,” said Steve duMont, president of GM Defense. “We do not begin with a blank sheet of paper. By transferring GM’s world-class engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing scale directly to the service member, we are transforming customer needs into mission-ready capability faster than ever before.”
As a reminder, GM Defense focuses on "integrated vehicles; power and propulsion; and autonomy and connectivity solutions to global defense, security and government markets." It proposes OEM quality and world-class manufacturing scale for rapid deployment of contracts.

Credit: DP World Dakar Port
By Alexander Whiteman
13 October 2026
Congestion along West Africa’s coast is exposing infrastructure that appears dramatically ill-suited to the region’s rapidly developing container market, with concerns that the level of investment, and its intended developments, are not where they need to be.
Last year, Drewry recorded a 19.4% year-on-year upturn in regional container throughput, reflecting the introduction of larger vessels on Asia-West Africa services, and The Loadstar’s reporting indicates developing trade between West Africa and Latin America.
Eirik Hooper, Drewry’s ports and terminals specialist, told The Loadstar : “The congestion appears to be the result of a mismatch between rapidly expanding vessel capacity, growing volumes and the ability of terminals and supporting logistics systems to process that cargo.”
He believes the source of this pressure is linked to introduction of 24,000 teu vessels on MSC’s Africa Express service, which began last April, and by May was calling at Lomé, Tema, Abidjan, and Kribi, although he warned problems vary considerably across ports.
According to Drewry, Doula operated last year at 102% utilisation, with volumes rising 48% year on year, while Conakry, Dakar, Lomé, and Pointe-Noire hovered between 81% and 84%. But pointing to Tema, Mr Hooper said simply seeing this as a terminal issue would not help.
The Ghanaian gateway experienced congestion of between four and seven days during the summer peak and is still hovering around the six-day mark, despite the country’s transport minister noting there had been significant improvements in terminal capacity this year.
But Mr Hooper said this came “without corresponding improvements to its supporting transport infrastructure”, adding: “The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority had already identified imports, empty containers and road congestion as principal contributors to delays.
“Consequently, it would be misleading to characterise Tema’s problems simply as a lack of terminal investment. The evidence instead points towards a mismatch between the scale of investment inside the terminal and investment outside it.
“Landside bottlenecks often determine effective terminal capacity meaning slow container evacuation, truck shortages, customs delays and inadequate off-dock storage contribute to high yard occupancy, reducing waterside productivity.”
Similar examples can be found; investment at Abidjan in additional yard equipment in 2025, did little to prevent average vessel wait times jumping from 0.4 days in February to 2.2 days by end of August, while Douala exceeding its handling capacity means it needs more.
“There are then two fundamentally different situations, modern terminals with insufficient hinterland connectivity versus terminals facing genuine operational constraints West African port congestion exposes gaps in infrastructure investment,” Mr Hooper added.
DP World chief executive and managing director for Africa, Mohammed Akoojee, seems to see a relatively obvious solution: combining terminal expansion with investment across the wider African supply chain.
Mr Akoojee told The Loadstar : “Addressing these challenges requires more than expanding terminals. Investment in modern equipment, deeper berths, roads, rail and inland logistics networks must go hand in hand to ensure cargo moves efficiently through the supply chain.”
For its part, DP World has invested $340m in modernising its Dakar terminal, increasing throughput from 265,000 teu in 2008 to 850,000 teu in 2025, with the operator noting that this has seen vessel wait times plummet from 35 hours to near zero.
However, he said that “even highly productive terminals” eventually encountered physical constraints, with this particularly true in cases where opportunities for further expansion are limited.
“Our $1.2bn investment in the new deepwater port of Ndayane builds on this progress, providing capacity for larger vessels and future trade growth. Ndayane will have an initial annual container-handling capacity of 1.2m teu in the first phase,” Mr Akoojee said.
This project forms part of a wider wave of port development across the region, including new terminals at Pointe-Noire, Banana, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and projects in Nigeria, alongside expansions at San Pedro in Ivory Coast, Takoradi in Ghana, and Luanda.
“With African trade expected to grow and shipping evolving, continued integrated investment in port and logistics infrastructure are essential; needs vary by market, but our focus remains developing capacity, improving efficiency and strengthening inland connectivity,” he added.

source_document.body:
Syndax Pharmaceuticals will no longer test Niktimvo for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, but the company’s work to expand the drug’s label in chronic graft-versus-host disease, for which it was approved in 2024, will continue.
Syndax Pharmaceuticals’ Niktimvo failed to significantly preserve lung function in a mid-stage study, prompting the company to discontinue the drug’s development in a chronic lung scarring disease.
In a bid to expand Niktimvo , which was approved in 2024 for chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD), into idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), Syndax ran the Phase 2 MAXPIRe study , enrolling 145 patients with the lung condition.
Without providing specific data, the biotech on Monday said that the monoclonal antibody, also called axatilimab, failed to meet the trial’s primary endpoint of slowing the annualized rate of decline in forced vital capacity—a measure of how much air a person can exhale—at 26 weeks.
Given the findings, Syndax is discontinuing development of axatilimab for IPF.
Syndax stocks have dipped from $16.55 at market close yesterday to $14.89 apiece in premarket trading Tuesday—a 10% drop.
MAXPIRe “was always a high risk, high-reward trial,” Mizuho Securities wrote in a Monday note, adding that Wall Street’s “confidence going into this readout was never really that high” since the trial was trying to unlock a novel therapeutic mechanism to potentially access a multi-billion-dollar market.
No new safety signals were observed in the trial, so Mizuho sees no readthrough to the GVHD program.
Treatment-emergent adverse events that led to discontinuation remained low in patients treated with axatilimab. Niktimvo is currently approved for patients who have undergone at least two prior lines of cGVHD treatment.
Syndax will continue two ongoing studies in this indication, testing combinations of Niktimvo with standard-of-care medicines as a potential first-line intervention. Results from one of these studies are expected later this year, while the other is set to read out in early 2028, according to the Monday announcement.
Syndax is developing Niktimvo in GVHD in partnership with Incyte under a September 2021 partnership that involved a $152 million upfront payment, plus up to $450 million in milestones. This alliance doesn’t extend to IPF, Mizuho said on Monday.
IPF is a chronic respiratory condition that scars the lungs, making it difficult for patients to breathe. Syndax proposed Niktimvo as a treatment for this condition based on the asset’s ability to target and block CSF-1R, a protein that regulates the survival and activity of immune cells—underlying players in the formation of scar tissue in the lungs. The FDA in April 2021 granted Niktimvo orphan drug status for IPF.
Elsewhere in the IPF arena, Bristol Myers Squibb reported on Monday that its LPA1 blocker admilparant significantly improved lung function at 52 weeks—an effect that was observed only with the asset’s 60-mg dose and not at the 120-mg dose. The lack of a dose-response effect prompted Leerink analysts to call the readout “mixed,” noting that while admilparant’s data could be enough to support an approval application, the high-dose miss “raises questions about its profile.”
